timing.summary: Acrylamide itself is gone within 3-4 days of a meal, so urinary markers reflect yesterday's cooking [tleg-goempel2017]. Haemoglobin adducts average the last few months because they ride on the red cell, and the health concern - cancer - plays out over decades, which is why no short intervention can show a benefit.

onset.text: Urinary mercapturic acid excretion rises within hours of an acrylamide-rich meal and is essentially complete in 72-96 hours [tleg-goempel2017]; haemoglobin adducts form in linear proportion to dose [tleg-fennell2005].

full.text: Adduct levels approach a plateau over the roughly 120-day life of the red cell, so a sustained change in cooking habits takes about 4 months to show fully in adducts; within-person adduct levels are otherwise stable over years [tleg-wilson2009]. The cancer endpoints that motivate concern accrue over decades.

after_stopping.text: Labelled acrylamide was cleared within 72-96 hours with no release from deep compartments [tleg-goempel2017], but adducts wash out only as the labelled red cells are replaced, over roughly 4 months. A measurable background excretion persisted on an acrylamide-minimised diet, implying the body makes some acrylamide itself - so you cannot get to zero [tleg-goempel2017].

frequency.text: Because exposure does not accumulate in tissue, what matters is the long-run average, not any single meal: an occasional batch of dark-roasted or well-browned food is irrelevant against the endogenous background [tleg-goempel2017]. Daily staples (coffee, bread, fried potato) dominate intake and therefore adducts [tleg-wilson2009].

timing.debate: The implication of the endogenous background is contested in practice: if the body generates 0.3-0.4 ug/kg/day of acrylamide regardless of diet [tleg-goempel2017], the achievable reduction from cooking changes is smaller than exposure-assessment models assume. Adducts also correlate only moderately (r about 0.3) with questionnaire intake, so studies disagree partly because they are measuring different time windows [tleg-wilson2009].

timing.summary: Air pollution acts on two clocks at once. Within 2 hours of a particle peak, heart attack risk rises [tleg-peters2001] and oxidative markers follow within hours to days [tleg-li2020pm]; over years, sustained differences in exposure change life expectancy [tleg-pope2009]. For sperm, the damaging exposure happened during the 0-90 days before the sample, with specific windows for specific pollutants [tleg-sun2020, tleg-russo2025].

onset.text: Myocardial infarction risk rose with fine particles in the previous 2 hours and again with the 24-hour average one day earlier [tleg-peters2001]; each 10 ug/m3 of short-term PM2.5 was associated with 1.6% higher malondialdehyde within days [tleg-li2020pm].

full.text: Cardiovascular and mortality risk reflects years of average exposure: a 10 ug/m3 lower PM2.5 over about two decades was associated with 0.61 more years of life expectancy [tleg-pope2009]. Semen effects reflect the full 74-90 day spermatogenic window [tleg-russo2025].

after_stopping.text: The acute component reverses within days once exposure falls, which is what purifier trials show [tleg-chen2015]. At population level, Dublin's coal ban was followed by a 15.5% fall in respiratory and 10.3% fall in cardiovascular deaths within months to a few years [tleg-clancy2002], though a larger follow-up and a reanalysis found much smaller or absent mortality effects [tleg-dockery2013, tleg-wittmaack2007].

frequency.text: What matters is cumulative dose plus avoiding peaks: both the acute (hours) and chronic (years) components are real, so reducing exposure on high-pollution days has a different (and faster) payoff than moving to cleaner air, which pays off over years [tleg-peters2001, tleg-pope2009].

sperm.late_start: A late start still helps: PM2.5 and ozone exposure during spermiation - the final days before release - was associated with lower count, concentration and motility, so even the last 2 weeks of reduced exposure acts on a sensitive stage [tleg-russo2025].
sperm.text: Distributed-lag analyses place the critical windows at development weeks 6-12 for PM10, weeks 10-11 for ozone and weeks 0-5 for SO2 [tleg-sun2020], and ozone during meiosis and spermiogenesis specifically affected morphology [tleg-russo2025]. Sperm DNA fragmentation rose after high-pollution periods within the same men [tleg-rubes2005].

egg.late_start: Ovarian stimulation is the most sensitive window identified, so reducing exposure in the 2 weeks of stimulation and up to retrieval is worth doing even if nothing was done earlier [tleg-gaskins2019].
egg.text: In 522 IVF cycles the association with failure was strongest for exposure during ovarian stimulation (42% higher odds of failing before retrieval per interquartile rise in NO2), not during later stages [tleg-gaskins2019].

timing.debate: The size and even existence of the fast population-level benefit is contested: the Dublin coal-ban analysis reported large mortality falls [tleg-clancy2002], the extended Irish analysis found respiratory but not cardiovascular or total mortality reductions [tleg-dockery2013], and a reanalysis attributed the original finding to influenza epidemics and secular trends [tleg-wittmaack2007]. For the egg, one real-world study linked NO2 to lower AMH [tleg-lamarca2020] while a 20-year cohort with repeated measurements found no association with AMH or age at menopause [tleg-zou2025].

timing.summary: A HEPA purifier is a tap, not a treatment: oxidative and inflammatory markers and blood pressure improve within 48 hours to a week of switching it on [tleg-chen2015, tleg-wang2021], and the benefit goes away when it is switched off. Nothing accumulates, so it has to run continuously to do anything.

onset.text: Forty-eight hours of real versus sham filtration cut indoor PM2.5 by 57% and lowered myeloperoxidase by 33% along with blood pressure [tleg-chen2015]; one week lowered urinary 8-isoprostane, exhaled nitric oxide and diastolic pressure [tleg-wang2021].

full.text: Pooled sham-controlled home trials lasting a median of 13.5 days found about a 4 mmHg fall in systolic blood pressure with no sign that longer studies did better [tleg-walzer2020], so the effect appears to plateau within about 2 weeks.

after_stopping.text: Crossover designs are the evidence: markers and blood pressure return toward baseline during sham periods, i.e. within days of filtration stopping [tleg-chen2015, tleg-wang2021].

frequency.text: Continuous operation in the rooms where you spend most time, especially the bedroom. Because the biological effect follows the exposure within days, intermittent use buys only intermittent benefit; filters also need maintenance to keep working.

sperm.late_start: Unknown. Filtration changes exposure the same day, but any semen effect would require the full spermatogenic cycle, and the only study to try it (a year of indoor purification in infertile men) found no improvement [tleg-paradisi2009].
sperm.text: Air-pollution exposure windows for sperm span the 90 days before ejaculation [tleg-sun2020], so a purifier would in principle need to run for that whole period; this has not been tested successfully [tleg-paradisi2009].

egg.late_start: Running a purifier only during ovarian stimulation targets the window with the strongest observational signal [tleg-gaskins2019], but no trial has tested this.
egg.text: Filtration lowers exposure immediately [tleg-chen2015]; whether that improves IVF outcomes has not been tested, and the one pregnancy trial of HEPA filters found no overall birth-weight benefit [tleg-barn2018].

timing.debate: How much the short-term marker changes mean is contested. One meta-analysis found a 4 mmHg systolic fall [tleg-walzer2020] and another found only 2.3 mmHg with no change in CRP or endothelial function and graded the certainty as very low, explicitly warning against strong claims [tleg-xia2021]; a third found 7% lower CRP and 13% lower IL-6 [tleg-wittkopp2022]. The only hard-outcome trial, HEPA filters through pregnancy in a highly polluted city, missed its primary endpoint [tleg-barn2018].

timing.summary: Burning things indoors acts within hours: a 4-hour wood-smoke exposure raised airway oxidative markers [tleg-barregard2008], and the exposure stops when the fire or burner does. Fixing the source works on two timescales - indoor NO2 falls within a week of replacing a gas stove [tleg-paulin2014], while symptom and health changes take a couple of months [tleg-sehgal2026].

onset.text: Four hours of 240-280 ug/m3 wood smoke raised malondialdehyde in exhaled breath condensate and alveolar nitric oxide [tleg-barregard2008]. HEPA/carbon purifiers cut kitchen NO2 immediately by 27%, and stove replacement by 51% at 3 months [tleg-paulin2014].

full.text: Exposure changes are complete within days to weeks of fixing the source [tleg-paulin2014]; clinical change takes longer - asthma control improved over the 2-3 months after gas stoves were swapped for electric [tleg-sehgal2026], and community wheeze reports fell over the winters after a wood-stove change-out [tleg-noonan2011].

after_stopping.text: Acute airway effects resolve within hours to a day of leaving the smoke [tleg-barregard2008]. Reverting to the old appliance restores the exposure immediately, since nothing is stored.

frequency.text: The dose is per burn, so the frequency of fires and gas cooking is what matters. Extraction that actually vents outdoors is necessary: in a randomized comparison, installing a ventilation hood over an unvented gas stove did not measurably lower NO2, while replacing the stove or adding HEPA/carbon purifiers did [tleg-paulin2014].

timing.debate: Whether modest wood-smoke exposures do anything systemic is contested: one chamber study found airway oxidative stress within hours [tleg-barregard2008] while another, at similar particle levels, found no effect on oxidative DNA damage, inflammation or microvascular function [tleg-forchhammer2012]. The gas-cooking and childhood-asthma literature is likewise disputed, with a systematic review by consultancy-affiliated authors judging 66 studies too weak for causal inference [tleg-li2023gas], while the stove-replacement study is uncontrolled and before-after [tleg-sehgal2026].

timing.summary: Thirty minutes is enough: passive smoke cut coronary flow velocity reserve in healthy young men from 4.4 to 3.4 in a single half-hour exposure [tleg-otsuka2001], and brief exposures produce 80-90% of the vascular and oxidative effect of active smoking [tleg-barnoya2005]. At population level, heart attack rates fell within the first year or two after smoking bans, although how big that effect really is remains disputed.

onset.text: Coronary endothelial dysfunction was measurable after a 30-minute exposure [tleg-otsuka2001]; platelet, endothelial and oxidative changes follow within minutes to hours [tleg-barnoya2005].

full.text: The acute vascular effect is maximal within hours; the 30% excess coronary risk reflects years of living or working in smoke [tleg-barnoya2005].

after_stopping.text: Acute vascular effects resolve over hours after leaving the exposure [tleg-otsuka2001]. At population level, myocardial infarction admissions fell 17% after public smoking bans, with a further 26% relative fall for each additional year after the ban [tleg-meyers2009], and Cochrane found the clearest effect for acute coronary syndrome admissions [tleg-frazer2016].

frequency.text: There is no safe dose and no schedule: each exposure produces its own acute effect, so avoidance is about eliminating episodes rather than reducing an average [tleg-otsuka2001, tleg-barnoya2005].

sperm.late_start: Removing the exposure helps from that day for vascular effects, but sperm formed during months of exposure cannot be unmade; one spermatogenic cycle is the lead time.
sperm.text: Extrapolated from spermatogenesis length rather than measured for passive smoke specifically; active smoking is associated with about 9 points more sperm DNA fragmentation, and passive exposure reproduces most of active smoking's oxidative effects [tleg-barnoya2005].

egg.late_start: Clearing the home of smoke even weeks before an IVF cycle removes exposure during the periovulatory and implantation window, which is where the IVF signal lies.
egg.text: In an IVF series, passive smokers had implantation (12.6% vs 25.0%) and pregnancy rates (20.0% vs 48.3%) as low as active smokers despite similar embryo quality, pointing at the peri-implantation period rather than earlier follicle growth [tleg-neal2005].

timing.debate: The speed and size of the population benefit is genuinely contested: a meta-analysis of local studies found a 17% drop in myocardial infarction after bans [tleg-meyers2009] and Cochrane found consistent cardiovascular improvement [tleg-frazer2016], but a US national analysis found no significant short-term decline and showed that, in small samples, large increases after a ban were as common as the published large decreases [tleg-shetty2010]. One study of women with modest exposure also found no difference in 8-isoprostane or oxidized LDL [tleg-sitihajar2018].

timing.summary: The filter works the day you install it, but your blood takes years to notice. Serum PFAS fall only about 13-26% a year once the contaminated supply is replaced [tleg-li2018pfas], so a point-of-use filter is an investment with a multi-year payback rather than a quick fix [tleg-cuffney2023].

onset.text: Water concentrations drop as soon as a working filter is in line [tleg-mackeown2024]; the first measurable change in serum takes months, because the body burden is leaving at 13-26% a year [tleg-li2018pfas].

full.text: Serum levels approach the new, lower steady state over several years: halving takes 2.7-5.3 years depending on the compound [tleg-li2018pfas]. Home-filter users in a contaminated county had lower serum levels of all seven PFAS measured, a cross-sectional snapshot of that slow process [tleg-cuffney2023].

after_stopping.text: If the filter is removed or left unmaintained, exposure resumes immediately and serum levels climb again; exhausted activated carbon can even release PFAS back into the water [tleg-mackeown2024].

frequency.text: Continuous use plus maintenance on schedule: the benefit comes from every glass, and a neglected carbon filter can be worse than none [tleg-mackeown2024]. Reverse osmosis and ion exchange remove more, and short-chain PFAS slip through more easily [tleg-mackeown2024].

sperm.late_start: Installing a filter a month before conception will not change serum PFAS measurably for that cycle; it is a long-horizon measure that also protects a later pregnancy and breastfeeding.
sperm.text: The lead time is set by PFAS elimination (half-lives of years) rather than by sperm development [tleg-li2018pfas].

timing.debate: Real-world filter performance is thinly evidenced: only five real-life point-of-use studies exist, performance varies with maintenance, and short-chain PFAS are poorly removed [tleg-mackeown2024]. The serum evidence is cross-sectional and cannot separate filter use from other habits [tleg-cuffney2023]. For microplastics there is no evidence that filtering changes any measured body burden [tleg-lane2026].

timing.summary: A single meal cooked in old fryer fat impaired endothelial function within 4 hours in one crossover trial [tleg-williams1999], and oxidized lipids from heated oil appear in chylomicrons within hours of eating [tleg-staprans1994]. There is no body store: the exposure and its effect are per-meal, while the cardiovascular associations reflect years of habit [tleg-qin2021].

onset.text: Four hours after a meal rich in fat taken from a commercial fryer, flow-mediated dilation fell from 5.9% to 0.8%, while the same meal with unused fat did nothing [tleg-williams1999]; oxidized lipids are measurable in postprandial chylomicrons within 2.5 hours [tleg-staprans1994].

full.text: Nothing accumulates from a single meal; the postprandial effect resolves within the same day, and the disease associations (22-37% more cardiovascular events in the highest fried-food category) reflect years of eating pattern [tleg-qin2021].

after_stopping.text: Endothelial function and postprandial oxidized lipids return to baseline within hours to a day; there is no lasting component to clear [tleg-williams1999, tleg-staprans1994].

frequency.text: Frequency is the whole exposure: each fried meal is its own hit, so the relevant quantity is how often you eat food cooked in heavily reused oil. Which oil and how long it has been heated also matters - repeatedly heated sunflower oil raised postprandial 8-OHdG while virgin olive oil did not [tleg-rangel2017].

timing.debate: The acute effect has failed to replicate: the same group that found impaired endothelial function after used-fryer fat later found no effect from olive or safflower oil used for 8 hours of deep frying, despite high levels of oxidation products [tleg-williams1999, tleg-williams2001]. The long-term associations also conflict: a meta-analysis found 22-37% more cardiovascular events with fried food [tleg-qin2021] while a large Spanish cohort frying in olive and sunflower oil found none [tleg-guallar2012].

timing.summary: Switching oil changes what forms in the pan tonight - there is no build-up phase and no washout. The only slow clocks are in the bottle and the fryer: oils degrade over hours of frying (olive oils lasted 24-27 hours versus 15 for a PUFA-rich blend) [tleg-casal2010] and over months of storage.

onset.text: Immediate: the oil you cook in determines the oxidation products in that meal, and the postprandial difference is measurable within hours - repeatedly heated sunflower oil raised postprandial oxidative-stress and DNA-repair markers while virgin olive oil did not [tleg-rangel2017].

full.text: No cumulative effect to reach; the practical 'full effect' is replacing habitual high-heat PUFA frying, which changes every subsequent meal [tleg-rangel2017, tleg-casal2010].

after_stopping.text: Reverting to a less stable oil restores the exposure with the next meal; nothing is retained [tleg-rangel2017].

frequency.text: Per cooking session. The useful schedule rules are about the oil's own clock: discard frying oil well before it darkens and smells (olive oils reached the 25% polar-compound limit after 24-27 hours of domestic deep-frying, a PUFA-rich blend after 15) [tleg-casal2010], and store oil cool and dark.

timing.debate: Whether the oil-stability difference matters for health is unresolved: postprandial marker trials favour virgin olive oil [tleg-rangel2017] and chemistry favours monounsaturated oils for frying [tleg-casal2010], but a large cohort frying in olive or sunflower oil found no difference in coronary events [tleg-guallar2012], and blood linoleic acid is associated with lower, not higher, cardiovascular risk [tleg-marklund2019].

timing.summary: The chemistry is per-meal and the biomarkers clear in a day - heterocyclic amines from a fried-meat meal are largely excreted within 24 hours [tleg-reistad1997] - but a high-AGE meal measurably impaired vascular function within 2-6 hours [tleg-negrean2007]. The cancer and metabolic risks attributed to browning build over years of habit, and the best controlled diet trials of 2-6 weeks found nothing.

onset.text: A high-AGE meal cut flow-mediated dilation by 36% at 2-6 hours in people with type 2 diabetes versus 21% for an identical low-AGE meal [tleg-negrean2007]; heterocyclic amines appear in urine the same day and are largely gone within 24 hours [tleg-reistad1997].

full.text: Two weeks of a low-AGE diet raised insulin sensitivity on clamp in one crossover trial [tleg-decourten2016], but 4-6 week trials found no effect [tleg-linkens2022, tleg-semba2014]. Colorectal adenoma associations with heterocyclic amine intake (OR about 1.20) reflect years of cooking habit [tleg-gongora2019].

after_stopping.text: Urinary HCA markers are gone within about a day [tleg-reistad1997] and the postprandial vascular effect resolves within hours [tleg-negrean2007]; cumulative cancer risk, by definition, does not reverse quickly.

frequency.text: Because nothing accumulates, it is the everyday cooking method that matters - the occasional charred steak is a rounding error against a daily habit of frying and grilling to well done. Lower-temperature and moist methods, shorter high-heat times and marinating all act on the same meal [tleg-salmon1997, tleg-smith2008].

egg.late_start: A late switch to gentler cooking changes exposure immediately, but there is no trial evidence that it changes egg quality at any notice.
egg.text: Serum and follicular-fluid AGEs were associated with fewer oocytes and lower ongoing pregnancy in an IVF cohort, and dietary AGE intake changes within days [tleg-negrean2007]; whether reducing it over a follicle-growth window (about 3-4 months) helps has not been tested.

timing.debate: The dietary-AGE story is the main dispute, and it is about duration as well as direction: a 2-week crossover found better insulin sensitivity on a low-AGE diet [tleg-decourten2016], while a 4-week randomized trial in 73 people [tleg-linkens2022] and a 6-week trial in healthy adults [tleg-semba2014] found no effect on insulin sensitivity, vascular function or inflammation despite confirmed differences in intake. Heterocyclic amine associations with adenoma are modest and based on intake estimation [tleg-gongora2019].

timing.summary: This is a one-off kitchen step with no biology to wait for: the marinade changes what forms during that cooking session, and the effect is over when the meal is. The only clock is the marinating time itself - 1 hour was enough for herb-spice marinades to cut heterocyclic amines 57-88% [tleg-smith2008], while beer marinades did better at 6 hours than at 2-4 [tleg-melo2008].

onset.text: Immediate and confined to the meal: a 1-hour herb-and-spice marinade cut total heterocyclic amines in grilled steak by 57-88% [tleg-smith2008], and a vinegar-lemon-garlic type marinade cut PhIP in grilled chicken by 92-99% [tleg-salmon1997].

full.text: Longer marinating helps up to a point: beer marinades cut heterocyclic amines by about 88% after 6 hours versus less at 2-4 hours [tleg-melo2008], and overnight teriyaki or turmeric-garlic marinades lowered PhIP and MeIQx [tleg-nerurkar1999].

after_stopping.text: Nothing persists: an unmarinated grill session produces the full complement of heterocyclic amines again [tleg-smith2008].

frequency.text: Only on the occasions you use high dry heat - that is the only time it does anything. Sugary marinades can backfire: a sugar-containing marinade cut PhIP by 92-99% but raised MeIQx more than ten-fold at long cooking times [tleg-salmon1997], and a honey barbecue sauce tripled PhIP [tleg-nerurkar1999].

timing.debate: All of this is food chemistry with no human health outcome, and the direction depends on the recipe: herb, spice, beer, wine and acid marinades lower heterocyclic amines [tleg-smith2008, tleg-melo2008], while sugar-rich marinades raise MeIQx several-fold [tleg-salmon1997] or PhIP three-fold [tleg-nerurkar1999]. No trial has measured whether any of it changes a biomarker in people, let alone cancer risk.

timing.summary: The gut chemistry changes within days - faecal N-nitroso compounds rise in proportion to red-meat intake under controlled feeding [tleg-bingham2002] - and plasma TMAO rises over about 4 weeks of daily red meat and falls again within 4 weeks of stopping [tleg-wang2019tmao]. The cancer risk that drives the IARC classification accrues over decades and has no short-term readout.

onset.text: Faecal apparent total N-nitroso compounds rose linearly with red meat from 0 to 420 g/day within days of controlled feeding [tleg-bingham2002]; white meat had no such effect.

full.text: Plasma and urinary TMAO roughly tripled after 4 weeks of a red-meat diet, through more precursor, more microbial conversion and less renal clearance [tleg-wang2019tmao]. Colorectal cancer risk, the basis of the Group 1 classification for processed meat, reflects years to decades of intake [tleg-bouvard2015, tleg-bastide2011].

after_stopping.text: TMAO returned to baseline within 4 weeks of stopping red meat [tleg-wang2019tmao], and faecal nitrosation markers fall as soon as intake does [tleg-bingham2002]. Cumulative cancer risk does not reverse on that timescale.

frequency.text: The measurable markers track current intake, not a lifetime store, so cutting back works whenever you do it and reverting undoes it within weeks [tleg-wang2019tmao]. White meat at the same quantity did not raise faecal nitrosation [tleg-bingham2002], so substitution rather than schedule is the lever.

timing.debate: Whether the slow clock justifies acting at all is disputed: IARC classifies processed meat as Group 1 and red meat as Group 2A [tleg-bouvard2015] and heme intake carries an 18% higher colon cancer risk [tleg-bastide2011], but the NutriRECS panel reviewed the same literature and issued weak recommendations that adults continue their current intake, judging the certainty of benefit from cutting back to be low [tleg-johnston2019]. The fast biomarkers (TMAO, faecal nitrosation) have never been shown to mediate the cancer risk.

timing.summary: Semen reflects the diet of the preceding 2-3 months, not of last week, because a sperm takes about 74-90 days to make. The processed-meat associations come from questionnaires covering the previous year [tleg-afeiche2014a, tleg-afeiche2014b], so one spermatogenic cycle is the minimum honest trial period - and no trial has been done.

onset.text: Not measured. No study has fed or withdrawn processed meat and followed semen over time; the association comes from cross-sectional and repeated-measures cohorts using food-frequency questionnaires [tleg-afeiche2014a, tleg-afeiche2014b].

full.text: Extrapolated from spermatogenesis: a complete change in the sperm population takes about 74-90 days, so changes in diet should be judged after roughly 3 months, as air-pollution window studies over the same 74-day window demonstrate [tleg-russo2025].

after_stopping.text: Not measured; by the same logic, going back to a high processed-meat diet would take about one spermatogenic cycle to show in semen. Nothing suggests a lasting effect after that.

frequency.text: No study has compared schedules. The quantity signal is in the top versus bottom quartile of habitual intake (about 1.7 percentage points fewer normal forms [tleg-afeiche2014a], and about 78 million fewer sperm per ejaculate in young men [tleg-afeiche2014b]), which implies average weekly intake over months rather than any single meal.

sperm.late_start: Starting 2-4 weeks before conception can only affect the last stages of maturation and epididymal transit; the cell divisions most plausibly affected happened 1-3 months earlier.
sperm.text: Lead time is set by the 74-90 day spermatogenic cycle, which is also the window over which environmental exposures have measurable semen effects [tleg-russo2025]. Unprocessed red meat was not associated with worse semen in the same cohorts [tleg-afeiche2014b].

timing.debate: The timing claim is entirely extrapolated: no intervention study exists. The association itself is contested - the young-men study's authors noted that it was strongest in men with under 2 days' abstinence and was driven by ejaculate volume, so residual confounding by abstinence time cannot be excluded [tleg-afeiche2014b], and the broader meat-and-health literature is disputed [tleg-johnston2019].

timing.summary: There is no effect on semen to time: in young men, unprocessed red meat showed no association with any semen measure, while processed meat did [tleg-afeiche2014b]. If you change intake anyway, judge the result after one spermatogenic cycle of about 74-90 days.

onset.text: No measurable semen effect to appear [tleg-afeiche2014b].

full.text: Not applicable. Any dietary change would need about 74-90 days to show in semen, by analogy with measured exposure windows for spermatogenesis [tleg-russo2025].

after_stopping.text: Not applicable: nothing to reverse [tleg-afeiche2014b].

frequency.text: No schedule evidence and no semen signal to act on [tleg-afeiche2014b]. Gut-level effects of red meat (faecal nitrosation, TMAO) are a separate question handled under [processed-red-meat] and do respond within days to weeks [tleg-bingham2002, tleg-wang2019tmao].

sperm.late_start: Nothing to start: no benefit has been shown from reducing unprocessed red meat for semen quality [tleg-afeiche2014b].
sperm.text: No measured time course exists because no effect has been demonstrated.

timing.debate: Whether unprocessed red meat is harmless for fertility is a question of absent evidence rather than conflicting evidence; the general-health debate about red meat is live, with IARC's Group 2A classification [tleg-bouvard2015] against the NutriRECS panel's weak recommendation to continue current intake [tleg-johnston2019].

timing.summary: Your blood changes in a fortnight and your fat changes over years. Plasma and red-cell linoleic acid shift within 2 weeks of changing intake and then plateau [tleg-hodson2014], whereas adipose tissue - where most of the body's linoleic acid sits - turns over with a triglyceride half-life of 200-270 days [tleg-strawford2004] and only correlated well with diet after 5-6 years in a long feeding trial [tleg-dayton1967].

onset.text: Plasma, erythrocyte and buccal-cell linoleic acid rose during the first 2 weeks of a high-linoleic diet and then stayed flat [tleg-hodson2014]; cholesteryl-ester fatty acids have an incorporation half-life of about 5 days [tleg-katan1997].

full.text: Different pools plateau at different times: cholesteryl esters in 4-8 weeks, erythrocytes at about 180 days (half-life 28 days), and adipose tissue still changing at 12 months [tleg-katan1997]. Adipose triglyceride half-life is 200-270 days [tleg-strawford2004] and bomb-carbon dating gives a mean adipose lipid age of about 1.6 years [tleg-arner2011], so full equilibration takes years - which is how US adipose linoleic acid rose 136% over half a century [tleg-guyenet2015].

after_stopping.text: Reversal follows the same pools in reverse: blood measures within weeks, adipose over years [tleg-katan1997, tleg-strawford2004]. In a 16-week crossover, adipose composition did not detectably change at all [tleg-hodson2014].

frequency.text: Average intake over months is what sets tissue composition, so day-to-day variation is irrelevant and short 'cleanses' do nothing to adipose stores [tleg-strawford2004]. Outcome trials of changing fat type ran 1-8 years, which is the honest timescale for judging effects [tleg-ramsden2016].

timing.debate: What the slow adipose clock means is contested. Higher blood linoleic acid was associated with lower cardiovascular disease and mortality across 30 cohorts [tleg-marklund2019], but recovered data from the Minnesota Coronary Experiment showed that replacing saturated fat with linoleic acid lowered cholesterol by 13.8% without any mortality benefit, and a pooled analysis of five trials was null [tleg-ramsden2016]. Both sides agree the exposure is slow: adipose biomarkers integrate years of intake [tleg-dayton1967, tleg-guyenet2015].

timing.summary: The lipid damage from trans fat shows up in 3 weeks: at 10% of energy it lowered HDL by 0.17 mmol/L and raised LDL within a 3-week feeding period [tleg-mensink1990]. Population-level removal paid off within about 3 years - Denmark's ban was followed by about 14 fewer cardiovascular deaths per 100,000 per year [tleg-restrepo2016], and New York's restrictions by 6-8% fewer heart attacks and strokes after 3 or more years [tleg-brandt2017].

onset.text: Blood lipid changes are measurable within the first weeks of a change in intake: a 3-week diet period was enough to show the full HDL and LDL effect [tleg-mensink1990].

full.text: Lipids reach a new steady state within about 3-4 weeks [tleg-mensink1990]; cardiovascular event rates in populations changed detectably 3 years after restrictions [tleg-brandt2017, tleg-restrepo2016]. Tissue trans fatty acids follow adipose turnover, a half-life of 200-270 days [tleg-strawford2004].

after_stopping.text: Lipid profile recovers over weeks once intake stops [tleg-mensink1990], while trans fatty acids already stored in adipose wash out over months to years, by the same kinetics as other fatty acids [tleg-strawford2004, tleg-arner2011].

frequency.text: This is a dose-average exposure rather than an acute one: what matters is habitual grams per day, since the lipid effect was demonstrated with 3 weeks of sustained intake [tleg-mensink1990]. There is no 'safe day' structure to exploit.

timing.debate: The feeding-trial lipid effect is uncontested; the speed of the population benefit is where interpretation varies, since both the Danish and New York analyses are natural experiments relying on synthetic or neighbouring controls and on the assumption that nothing else changed in the same 3-year window [tleg-restrepo2016, tleg-brandt2017].

timing.summary: CRP is a fast-moving marker: it falls within weeks to a few months of treating a source of inflammation - about 0.37 mg/L within 1-3 months of periodontal therapy [tleg-demmer2013] and about 0.13 mg/L per kilogram of weight lost [tleg-selvin2007]. The clinical payoff is much slower: lowering inflammation with canakinumab cut cardiovascular events by 15% over a median 3.7 years [tleg-ridker2017].

onset.text: Marker changes appear within weeks: periodontal treatment lowered CRP measurably at the earliest post-treatment measurement, typically 1-3 months [tleg-demmer2013], and statins cut CRP by 37% within the treatment period [tleg-ridker2008].

full.text: CRP reductions plateau over 1-6 months with the treated source [tleg-demmer2013, tleg-selvin2007], but the event reduction from targeting inflammation accrued over a median 3.7 years in CANTOS [tleg-ridker2017].

after_stopping.text: Markers rebound quickly when the suppression stops: CRP and IL-6 rose above treated levels within 3-7 days of abruptly stopping a statin, independently of LDL [tleg-li2006statin]. Untreated sources of inflammation (gums, visceral fat) resume driving oxidant production as soon as they return [tleg-mittal2014].

frequency.text: Inflammation responds to continuous rather than episodic measures, because the mediators turn over in hours to days: activated neutrophils and macrophages generate oxidants while the stimulus is present, and ROS and NF-kB amplify each other [tleg-mittal2014]. The practical lever is removing sources (gum disease, excess adiposity, smoke) rather than timing a treatment.

timing.debate: Whether CRP is a target or just a thermometer is the long-running dispute. CANTOS lowered CRP without changing lipids and reduced events, supporting causality [tleg-ridker2017], but only one of three doses met the significance threshold and fatal infections increased. Weight-loss and periodontal CRP reductions are consistent [tleg-selvin2007, tleg-demmer2013], yet trials lowering CRP in those ways have not demonstrated event reductions.

timing.summary: Periodontal treatment gets worse before it gets better: flow-mediated dilation fell and inflammatory markers rose 24 hours after intensive treatment, then endothelial function was better than controls at 60 days and clearly better at 180 days [tleg-tonetti2007]. HbA1c in people with diabetes falls by about 0.4 percentage points by 3-4 months and the benefit is still there at 12 months [tleg-simpson2022].

onset.text: A transient worsening first: 24 hours after intensive periodontal treatment, flow-mediated dilation was 1.4% lower and endothelial-activation markers higher than with routine care [tleg-tonetti2007]. Benefit emerges from about 1-2 months: CRP was about 0.37 mg/L lower at the earliest post-treatment measurement, typically 1-3 months [tleg-demmer2013], and FMD was 0.9% better at 60 days [tleg-tonetti2007].

full.text: By 180 days, flow-mediated dilation was 2.0% better than control care [tleg-tonetti2007]; HbA1c fell 0.43 percentage points at 3-4 months, 0.30 at 6 months and 0.50 at 12 months [tleg-simpson2022], and one 12-month trial found 0.6 points [tleg-daiuto2018]. Oxidative markers in saliva and gingival fluid improve over the same months [tleg-dasilva2018].

after_stopping.text: Not directly measured, but periodontitis recurs without maintenance, and the systemic markers track the periodontal state - the improvement in endothelial function correlated with the improvement in periodontal health [tleg-tonetti2007]. Untreated periodontitis is associated with persistently lower antioxidant capacity and higher malondialdehyde [tleg-liu2014].

frequency.text: Daily home care plus scheduled professional maintenance: the trials deliver an intensive course and then maintenance, and the systemic benefit tracks sustained periodontal health rather than the single treatment episode [tleg-tonetti2007, tleg-simpson2022]. Expect a bad 24-48 hours after intensive treatment.

timing.debate: The metabolic benefit is contested on both size and reality. Cochrane found a 0.43-point HbA1c reduction at 3-4 months from 30 trials with moderate certainty [tleg-simpson2022] and a UK trial found 0.6 points at 12 months [tleg-daiuto2018], but the large multicentre US Diabetes and Periodontal Therapy Trial was stopped for futility with no HbA1c difference at 6 months despite improved periodontal measures [tleg-engebretson2013]. The CRP effect is small and only seen against no-treatment controls, not active comparators [tleg-demmer2013].

timing.summary: NSAIDs act on different systems at completely different speeds. Around ovulation they can block follicle rupture within the same cycle, and ovulation returns in the next cycle after stopping [tleg-micu2011, tleg-smith1996]; muscle adaptation is blunted over 8 weeks of training [tleg-lilja2018]; and testicular hormone changes appear with daily dosing over weeks [tleg-kristensen2018].

onset.text: Ovulatory effects within a single cycle: periovulatory rofecoxib delayed follicular rupture beyond 48 hours after the LH peak in 4 of 6 women in the treated cycle [tleg-pall2001], and continuous NSAIDs produced luteinized unruptured follicles in 35.6% of cycles [tleg-micu2011]. Training adaptation is measurably blunted by 8 weeks [tleg-lilja2018].

full.text: The hypertrophy penalty accumulated over 8 weeks of training (quadriceps volume +3.7% on ibuprofen 1,200 mg/day versus +7.5% on low-dose aspirin) [tleg-lilja2018]; hormonal changes developed with continued daily dosing [tleg-kristensen2018]; ovulatory suppression is dose-dependent and present while the drug is taken [tleg-jesam2014].

after_stopping.text: Ovulation recovers in the next cycle: three women with recurrent luteinized unruptured follicles on NSAIDs ovulated normally in the cycle after stopping [tleg-smith1996], and cycles normalised after an 18-day meloxicam regimen ended [tleg-jesam2014]. Muscle adaptation presumably resumes, but this was not measured.

frequency.text: Dose and continuity matter more than any clever schedule. Continuous periovulatory dosing is what caused unruptured follicles, and the COX-2-selective etoricoxib was the main culprit while ibuprofen 1,600 mg/day caused none [tleg-micu2011]; in older adults, 12 weeks of 1.2 g/day ibuprofen or 4 g/day acetaminophen during training did not blunt and may have helped muscle gains [tleg-trappe2011]. Occasional single doses outside the fertile window are a different exposure from daily use.

sperm.late_start: Stopping daily NSAIDs weeks before conception removes the hormonal effect, which is reversible, but any effect already imprinted on developing sperm would take a spermatogenic cycle to clear.
sperm.text: The measured effect is endocrine (raised LH, lower testosterone/LH ratio) rather than on sperm counts [tleg-kristensen2018]; the 90-day figure is extrapolated from spermatogenesis length, not measured.

egg.late_start: Two weeks is enough: the effect is on follicle rupture in the current cycle, so stopping before the periovulatory window restores ovulation in that cycle [tleg-pall2001, tleg-smith1996].
egg.text: NSAIDs act locally on COX-2-dependent follicle rupture, so the sensitive window is the few days around the LH surge [tleg-pall2001, tleg-micu2011], and use around conception was also associated with a 1.89-fold higher miscarriage risk, with a dose-response by duration [tleg-li2018nsaid].

timing.debate: Effects depend on who is taking them: maximal over-the-counter ibuprofen halved hypertrophy in young adults [tleg-lilja2018], while the same doses did not blunt and appeared to enhance gains in older adults over 12 weeks [tleg-trappe2011]. Ovulatory blockade is drug-specific - mostly etoricoxib, with none on ibuprofen 1,600 mg/day [tleg-micu2011] - and even at the highest meloxicam dose over 20% of women ovulated normally [tleg-jesam2014]. The miscarriage association comes from an observational cohort with acetaminophen users as an indication control [tleg-li2018nsaid].

timing.summary: Every dose draws on glutathione within hours, since therapeutic doses of 600-1200 mg speed cysteine and glutathione turnover [tleg-lauterburg1987]. Daily 4 g raises ALT above three times normal in 31-44% of healthy adults within 2 weeks [tleg-watkins2006], and - importantly for timing - those elevations resolve by day 40 even if dosing continues [tleg-heard2014].

onset.text: Glutathione turnover rises within hours of a single therapeutic dose [tleg-lauterburg1987]. At 4 g/day, ALT elevations appear within 4-14 days [tleg-watkins2006, tleg-heard2014].

full.text: The liver-enzyme signal peaks within the first 2-3 weeks and then adapts: 77% of people on 4 g/day had no or only transient ALT elevation by day 16, and 47 of the 48 with raised ALT at day 16 normalised by day 40 while still taking the drug [tleg-heard2014].

after_stopping.text: ALT elevations resolve over days to a few weeks after stopping, and often lag behind the drug's disappearance from blood [tleg-watkins2006]. The glutathione drain itself is per dose and ends with the dose [tleg-lauterburg1987].

frequency.text: The exposure is per dose, so occasional use and continuous maximal use are different exposures: 4 g/day is where the enzyme signal appears [tleg-watkins2006], and that signal attenuates with continued dosing [tleg-heard2014]. In older adults, 4 g/day for 12 weeks during resistance training did not impair muscle gains [tleg-trappe2011].

sperm.late_start: No lead time has been established; the glutathione effect is per dose and ends with the dose [tleg-lauterburg1987].
sperm.text: No human study has measured semen outcomes against timing of acetaminophen use, so no window can be given.

egg.late_start: No evidence supports stopping ahead of conception for egg quality; the recognised concerns are about exposure during pregnancy, i.e. after conception.
egg.text: No measured time course for egg outcomes exists; in the miscarriage cohort acetaminophen users served as the indication control group rather than showing the NSAID-associated risk [tleg-li2018nsaid].

timing.debate: The clinical meaning of the fast ALT rise is disputed: it appears in a third to a half of healthy adults within 2 weeks [tleg-watkins2006], yet it resolves during continued dosing and no participant developed liver dysfunction [tleg-heard2014], which argues for adaptation rather than progressive injury. Whether the per-dose glutathione cost matters at ordinary intermittent doses has not been tested on any clinical outcome [tleg-lauterburg1987].

timing.summary: Acid suppression has a fast microbiological effect and a slow nutritional one: specific gut taxa shift within 4 weeks [tleg-freedberg2015], while magnesium deficiency appeared after a median 5.5 years of use [tleg-hess2012] and B12 deficiency is associated with 2 or more years [tleg-lam2013]. Stopping has its own clock: magnesium recovers within about 4 days, but rebound acid symptoms appear in the weeks after withdrawal and can be mistaken for the original problem [tleg-reimer2009].

onset.text: Four weeks of high-dose omeprazole reproducibly increased Enterococcaceae and Streptococcaceae and decreased Clostridiales without changing overall diversity [tleg-freedberg2015]. Nutrient effects start much later - hypomagnesaemia onset ranged from 14 days to 13 years with a median of 5.5 years [tleg-hess2012].

full.text: Nutrient depletion accrues with duration: B12 deficiency was associated with 2 or more years of use and with higher doses [tleg-lam2013], and the magnesium cases clustered around 5.5 years [tleg-hess2012]. Microbiome changes appear established by 4-8 weeks [tleg-freedberg2015, tleg-imhann2016].

after_stopping.text: Magnesium recovered within about 4 days of stopping and fell again within about 4 days of re-challenge [tleg-hess2012]. But 8 weeks of a PPI caused clinically relevant acid-related symptoms in 21-22% of previously healthy volunteers during the 4 weeks after withdrawal, versus 2-7% on placebo - so expect 2-4 weeks of rebound [tleg-reimer2009].

frequency.text: Duration, not dosing pattern, is what the harm signals track [tleg-lam2013, tleg-hess2012], so the practical rule is the shortest course that does the job and periodic review. Tapering matters because of rebound hypersecretion in the weeks after stopping [tleg-reimer2009].

sperm.late_start: A late stop may not be enough: the association was with use 6-12 months before the semen analysis, not with use in the preceding 6 months, which is the opposite of a short-lag effect [tleg-huijgen2016].
sperm.text: In a primary-care registry, PPI use 6-12 months before semen analysis carried threefold higher odds of a low total motile count while recent use did not [tleg-huijgen2016] - an unexplained pattern that, taken at face value, implies a lead time of 6-12 months rather than one spermatogenic cycle.

timing.debate: The long-term harms are contested. Observational studies link 2 or more years of use to B12, iron and magnesium deficiency [tleg-lam2013, tleg-hess2012] and to large microbiome shifts [tleg-imhann2016], but the randomized COMPASS trial of 3 years of pantoprazole found no excess harm apart from slightly more enteric infections, and the controlled microbiome study found taxon shifts without any loss of diversity [tleg-freedberg2015]. The semen association has a biologically odd lag that its own authors could not explain [tleg-huijgen2016].

timing.summary: A short course does its damage in 3-4 days and most of it repairs within about 6 weeks, but not all of it: after a 4-day broad-spectrum cocktail, nine common species were still undetectable at 180 days [tleg-palleja2018], and a 7-day clindamycin course left Bacteroides diversity altered for up to 2 years [tleg-jernberg2007].

onset.text: Diversity collapses within 3-4 days of starting the drug [tleg-dethlefsen2011], and a 4-day cocktail wiped out much of the gut community [tleg-palleja2018].

full.text: The disruption is complete by the end of a typical course; the open question is recovery rather than onset [tleg-palleja2018, tleg-dethlefsen2011].

after_stopping.text: Recovery starts within a week of the last dose and reaches near-baseline at about 1.5 months, but nine common species were still missing at 180 days [tleg-palleja2018]; repeated ciprofloxacin courses left communities stabilised in an altered state [tleg-dethlefsen2011], and clindamycin effects on Bacteroides clones and resistance genes persisted up to 2 years [tleg-jernberg2007].

frequency.text: Each course carries its own incomplete recovery, and repeated courses do not simply repeat the same curve - the second ciprofloxacin course produced a different and less complete recovery than the first [tleg-dethlefsen2011]. Spacing courses does not restore what is lost [tleg-palleja2018].

sperm.late_start: Unknown: no study links antibiotic timing to semen outcomes. If a course is clinically needed, take it.
sperm.text: No measured semen time course exists; the 90-day figure is simply one spermatogenic cycle and is extrapolated, not evidence-based.

timing.debate: How much of the microbiome really fails to come back, and whether it matters, is unsettled: one study found near-complete recovery in 6 weeks with nine species missing at 6 months [tleg-palleja2018], another found persistent altered states and incomplete recovery between individuals [tleg-dethlefsen2011], and a third found 2-year persistence of resistance genes and clonal shifts [tleg-jernberg2007]. What helps recovery is also contested: probiotics delayed and left incomplete the mucosal recovery compared with spontaneous recovery, while autologous faecal transplant restored it within days [tleg-suez2018].

timing.summary: Lipid and oxidation markers move within 2-6 weeks - LDL, oxidized LDL and F2-isoprostanes all fall in the first month [tleg-decaterina2002] and blood CoQ10 halves within 14-30 days on high-dose atorvastatin [tleg-rundek2004]. Clinical benefit needs about 2.5 years to prevent one cardiovascular event per 100 people treated [tleg-yourman2021], while the excess of muscle symptoms is concentrated in the first year [tleg-ctt2022].

onset.text: LDL cholesterol and urinary F2-isoprostanes fell within the first month of simvastatin [tleg-decaterina2002]; blood CoQ10 fell significantly by day 14 on atorvastatin 80 mg and halved by day 30 [tleg-rundek2004]; CRP fell 37% in JUPITER [tleg-ridker2008].

full.text: Biomarkers plateau within 4-8 weeks; event reduction keeps accruing - 2.5 years to avoid one major event per 100 treated, but only 0.8 years per 500 treated [tleg-yourman2021], and in a high-risk trial events were reduced 44% over a median 1.9 years [tleg-ridker2008].

after_stopping.text: LDL returns toward baseline over about 2-6 weeks, and inflammatory markers rebound faster than lipids: CRP and IL-6 rose above treated levels by days 3 and 7 after abrupt withdrawal, despite unchanged LDL [tleg-li2006statin]. Five days off statins also raised circulating endothelial progenitor cells without an inflammatory rebound in a diabetic cohort [tleg-decaterina2002].

frequency.text: Daily dosing is what the trials used, and the first year is when muscle complaints cluster [tleg-ctt2022], so a planned re-trial after a break is informative. Statin-associated muscle symptoms are mostly not caused by the drug: statins produced only a 7% relative excess in year 1 (about 11 events per 1,000 person-years) and none afterwards, meaning over 90% of reported muscle symptoms were not due to the statin [tleg-ctt2022].

timing.debate: Two timing debates. First, muscle symptoms: individual-participant data show the excess is small and confined to year 1 [tleg-ctt2022], which conflicts with the clinical impression of persistent statin myalgia. Second, CoQ10: blood levels clearly fall within weeks [tleg-rundek2004], but trials of CoQ10 for statin muscle symptoms disagree, with one meta-analysis finding benefit [tleg-qu2018] and the broader literature unresolved. Whether the post-withdrawal CRP rebound translates into clinical risk is also unproven [tleg-li2006statin].

timing.summary: These drugs act unusually fast for a cardiovascular medicine - the benefit in DAPA-HF was statistically significant by 28 days [tleg-berg2021] - and unusually persistently, with cardiorenal benefit continuing for up to 12 months after the drug was stopped [tleg-empakidney2025]. The risk clock is faster still: euglycaemic ketoacidosis has followed a single dose or one week of a ketogenic diet [tleg-mistry2021].

onset.text: In DAPA-HF the reduction in cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure reached statistical significance by 28 days after randomization [tleg-berg2021]. The hazard - ketoacidosis at near-normal glucose - can appear within days of starting the drug or of starting a very-low-carbohydrate diet on it [tleg-mistry2021].

full.text: Benefit continues to accrue over the 2-3 years of the major trials [tleg-berg2021, tleg-empakidney2025]; the proposed mechanisms, including reduced oxidative stress, are largely preclinical and have no measured human time course [tleg-cowie2020].

after_stopping.text: Unusually, the effect outlives the drug: after empagliflozin was stopped, the cardiorenal benefit persisted for up to about 12 months (post-trial hazard ratio 0.87) before the groups converged [tleg-empakidney2025].

frequency.text: Daily dosing as trialled. The timing point that matters practically is dietary: do not start a ketogenic or very-low-carbohydrate diet while taking one of these drugs without medical supervision, because euglycaemic ketoacidosis has developed within a week of doing so, and even after the drug was stopped [tleg-mistry2021].

timing.debate: The redox part of the story is the contested part: lower oxidative stress is one of several proposed explanations for the cardiorenal benefit, but that evidence is largely mechanistic rather than human time-course data [tleg-cowie2020]. The post-trial persistence is also open to interpretation, since 40-43% of both groups took open-label SGLT2 inhibitors during follow-up [tleg-empakidney2025].

timing.summary: One unprotected exposure switches on collagen-degrading enzymes within hours and raises collagen breakdown by 58%, and with repeated exposures that enzyme activity stays up for about 7 days [tleg-fisher1997]. What accumulates from those episodes is structural and effectively permanent: identical twins with more sun exposure look older [tleg-guyuron2009], and skin cancer risk reflects decades.

onset.text: Matrix metalloproteinases are induced within hours of a single UV exposure, with collagen breakdown up 58% [tleg-fisher1997].

full.text: With repeated exposure, MMP activity remains elevated for about 7 days, so frequent exposures keep skin in a continuously degradative state [tleg-fisher1997]. Visible photoageing accumulates over years to decades [tleg-guyuron2009], and particulate air pollution adds to the same extrinsic ageing score [tleg-vierkotter2010].

after_stopping.text: The enzymatic response subsides over about a week once exposure stops [tleg-fisher1997], but the structural damage does not reverse on its own - which is why prevention trials measure effects over years and why the only partial reversal comes from treatment, not time [tleg-hughes2013].

frequency.text: Because MMP induction persists about 7 days, exposures more often than weekly keep the degradative state continuous [tleg-fisher1997]. There is no threshold below which repeated unprotected midday exposure stops contributing; protection has to be routine rather than occasional [tleg-hughes2013].

timing.debate: The acute molecular response is well measured [tleg-fisher1997]; what is debated is attribution of long-term ageing, since observational twin and cohort studies cannot fully separate sun from smoking, weight and pollution, all of which independently predicted older appearance or worse extrinsic ageing scores [tleg-guyuron2009, tleg-vierkotter2010].

timing.summary: This is the clearest example in the group of a benefit that keeps growing and then outlives the habit. Daily sunscreen for 4.5 years produced no detectable increase in photoageing and 24% less ageing than discretionary use [tleg-hughes2013]; squamous-cell tumour rates were still about 40% lower 8 years after the trial ended [tleg-vanderpols2006], and melanomas were halved over the following decade [tleg-green2011].

onset.text: Protection against the acute insult is immediate - tretinoin and sunscreen both act on the same MMP induction that starts within hours of exposure [tleg-fisher1997]. Visible improvement in photoageing scores was reported from week 12 of daily use, though in an uncontrolled study [tleg-randhawa2016].

full.text: The randomized photoageing difference was measured over 4.5 years [tleg-hughes2013], and squamous-cell tumour rates fell 39% over the same trial [tleg-green1999]. The cancer benefit kept growing after the trial: SCC still about 40% lower at 8 years post-trial [tleg-vanderpols2006] and melanoma halved at 10 years [tleg-green2011].

after_stopping.text: Remarkably, the benefit persisted after the enforced daily use ended: both the SCC reduction (8 years) and the melanoma reduction (10 years) were measured in the post-trial period, because prevented DNA damage cannot come back [tleg-vanderpols2006, tleg-green2011]. New unprotected exposure, of course, starts accumulating again.

frequency.text: Daily is what was tested and daily is what worked: the trial compared daily application with discretionary use, and only the daily arm showed the photoageing and tumour benefits [tleg-hughes2013, tleg-green1999]. Discretionary use was the comparator, not a second effective schedule.

timing.debate: The melanoma result is contested. The trial follow-up found melanomas halved [tleg-green2011], but a meta-analysis of observational studies found no overall protective association between sunscreen use and melanoma, attributing the discrepancy to confounding by sun sensitivity and exposure behaviour [tleg-rueegg2019]. The trial's photoageing outcome also had missing data and modest power [tleg-hughes2013].

timing.summary: Retinoids are slow to work and need maintenance: 16 weeks of daily tretinoin improved 14 of 15 treated faces versus none on vehicle [tleg-weiss1988], improvement continued or held through 48 weeks [tleg-olsen1997a], and after that three applications a week maintained it while once a week did less well and stopping led to partial regression [tleg-olsen1997b].

onset.text: Clinical improvement becomes evident over about 16 weeks of daily use [tleg-weiss1988]; the protective molecular effect is faster, with tretinoin pretreatment blocking 70-80% of UV-induced MMP induction [tleg-fisher1997].

full.text: Benefit continued to build to 24-48 weeks of daily use, with side effects becoming less common in the second half [tleg-olsen1997a]; retinol 0.4% applied up to three times weekly for 24 weeks reduced fine wrinkles even in people with a mean age of 87 [tleg-kafi2007].

after_stopping.text: Partial regression: in the 24 weeks after 48 weeks of daily tretinoin, people who stopped tended to lose their improvement, while three-times-weekly users held or improved [tleg-olsen1997b].

frequency.text: This is the one factor in the group with a direct schedule comparison. Daily to build, then three times a week to maintain - once a week was clearly weaker and stopping lost ground, and side effects tracked application frequency [tleg-olsen1997b]. Retinol at 0.4% worked at up to three times weekly from the start [tleg-kafi2007].

timing.debate: Retinoids treat appearance, not cancer: a trial of 1,131 high-risk veterans found topical 0.1% tretinoin for 1.5-5.5 years did not reduce basal-cell or invasive squamous-cell carcinoma or actinic keratosis counts [tleg-weinstock2012], so the fast molecular protection against UV-induced collagenase [tleg-fisher1997] does not translate into cancer prevention.

timing.summary: The skin reservoir fills fast and empties slowly for a topical: L-ascorbic acid saturates skin levels after three daily applications and then disappears with a tissue half-life of about 4 days [tleg-pinnell2001]. Visible change is a different, much slower matter - small vehicle-controlled trials assessed benefit at 3 and 6 months [tleg-humbert2003, tleg-correia2023].

onset.text: Skin levels saturate after about three daily applications [tleg-pinnell2001]; measurable antioxidant photoprotection is present once the reservoir is loaded, and adding ferulic acid to 15% vitamin C plus 1% vitamin E doubled that protection in skin [tleg-lin2005].

full.text: Clinically visible smoothing and pigment change were assessed at 3 and 6 months of daily use in the vehicle-controlled trials [tleg-humbert2003], and the systematic review of 7 trials in 139 volunteers used similar 3-6 month timeframes [tleg-correia2023].

after_stopping.text: The skin reservoir falls with a half-life of about 4 days, so most of the loaded vitamin C is gone within 1-2 weeks of stopping [tleg-pinnell2001]; whether the clinical gains fade as fast has not been measured.

frequency.text: Daily is the practical schedule and the one used in trials, but the kinetics suggest why: three consecutive daily applications are needed to saturate skin, and levels then decay with a 4-day half-life, so skipping several days lets the reservoir drain [tleg-pinnell2001]. Formulation matters more than frequency - it must be L-ascorbic acid below pH 3.5, best around 20% [tleg-pinnell2001].

timing.debate: The pharmacokinetics are from pig skin rather than people [tleg-pinnell2001], and the clinical evidence is thin: 7 small vehicle-controlled trials with 139 volunteers in total, with the reviewers calling for better studies and noting the ideal concentration is unresolved [tleg-correia2023]. The photoprotection data are also laboratory measurements rather than clinical outcomes [tleg-lin2005].

timing.summary: There is no credible time course to report, because there is no established effect: Cochrane could draw no conclusions from the three small trials (212 participants) of ozone therapy for its best-studied indication, diabetic foot ulcers [tleg-liu2015ozone]. Meanwhile ozone's measured biology is that of an acute airway oxidant, where exposure effects are a matter of hours.

onset.text: Not measured for any claimed benefit [tleg-liu2015ozone]. As an inhaled oxidant, ozone's effects on airway and systemic oxidative markers are acute, within hours of exposure, like other oxidant air pollutants [tleg-li2020pm].

full.text: Not measured: no trial establishes a plateau because no benefit has been established [tleg-liu2015ozone].

after_stopping.text: Not measured [tleg-liu2015ozone].

frequency.text: No schedule can be recommended: the trials are too few, too small and at high risk of bias to support any dosing interval [tleg-liu2015ozone].

timing.debate: Proponents frame ozone exposure as hormetic - a brief oxidant stress that triggers adaptive antioxidant responses - but the only systematic evidence base, Cochrane's review of its best-studied use, found three small trials at high or unclear risk of bias and no firm conclusions [tleg-liu2015ozone]. Ozone is simultaneously regulated as a harmful air pollutant whose exposure raises oxidative markers [tleg-li2020pm], and no study has reconciled the two framings with a measured time course.
